rubric.md.text:
# Three-arm natural engineering trial rubric

Freeze these checks before reading new outputs. The trial uses the same G1 and G2 owner business requirements, four initial Python modules, official DeepSeek Flash, evaluation checkpoints and completion caps across arms. Standard with a process checklist receives additional guidance deliberately. Evaluate all arms using the same artifact criteria regardless of documentation filenames, style, or tool vocabulary.

| Dimension | Evidence and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed functionality | G1 18 and G2 21 original black-box cases. Report first time with all cases green, scores at the aligned checkpoint and at the terminal snapshot. Report G2 applicable previous cases and new cases separately. Passing source is distinct from agent completion. |
| Quality beyond fixed tests | Run predeclared supplementary cases in the existing WSL bubblewrap evaluator. Core cases cover invalid environment input shapes, invalid retain data in plan and rollback, valid replay under quota and denial above quota after filtering, and production freeze with malformed graph/budget. Report exploratory transitive retention across an unapplied middle node separately due potential ambiguity. |
| Architecture | Score actual imports 4/4 and transport/I/O boundaries 4/4 from the original independent AST evaluator. In a separate manual review, check whether any actual artifact describes the split between entry, policy, journal and planner, rollout/rollback, and relevant current checks accurately. Wrong facts and obsolete decisions are tracked even when all fixed tests pass. No special filename, headings, JSON examples or document count is needed for credit. |
| Necessary source comments | Look for colocated comments or docstrings that explain real decisions, not just code restatements. Four anchors are replay identity and accounting, deterministic topology and reversed full-order rollback, fail-closed environment and budget checks, and G2 retention closure/filtering. Credit accurate explanations with file/line plus behavior evidence. At G1, retention is not yet applicable. Avoid using line or comment count as a quality score. |
| Maintainability | List line counts as context only. Examine source for duplicated graph logic, unused or mismatched paths, major interface/ownership changes and unnecessary coupling. Executed correctness and source structure remain separate. |
| Continuity and drift | Confirm a distinct G2 session, actual original directory if available, hash-identical carried G1 source and agent-authored project artifacts, and whether G2 consumed them when observable. Check current goal changes appear in functional and written outputs and stale G1 rules do not remain active. A frozen-copy continuation or a harness-created summary cannot establish original-directory autonomous continuity. |
| Review effectiveness | For an explicit finding or correction, record whether exact old/new artifact and requirement support it. Distinguish independently reproducible defect and fix, false rejection, repeated tool/format error, and unresolved ownership. Blank review logs never imply perfect quality. |
| Completion and usage | At the aligned and terminal checkpoints, report distinct source-pass, native-stage completion and independent whole-artifact status. Aggregate provider-reported total, uncached input, cache reads and output per arm. Cache hit is reads divided by total input. Missing usage is unknown. First-turn dismissal, cancellation and model/host infrastructure problems remain separate states. |

Only user-authored business constraints, independent output checks, and artifacts demonstrably written by the tested mode establish outcomes. Report unavoidable Building-loop-only host fixtures and their digest as input differences. Avoid collapsing the dimensions into a single grade in the first matched pair.

reviewer-notes.md.text:
# Independent source and handoff review

## First stage final snapshots

- Both ordinary standard arms finished 18/18. Their G1 artifacts contain only owner-provided project text and four implementation files. No model-authored G1 project documents or Python tests were captured. Both second sessions nonetheless recovered the carried four sources by reading each of them.
- In r-6ABuMo ordinary G1, graph validation and topology sit in `journal.py:65–98`. The common SPEC gives graph/order to planner. The local import inventory still passes 4/4, so this responsibility violation illustrates why import direction and actual module responsibility need separate measures. G1 source annotations were terse and described function output without an adjacent rationale for plan accounting/reverse rollback. Its G2 source does explain these rules in `planner.py:58–68` and describes the production freeze in `policy.py:31–32`.
- In r-AErMFD ordinary G1, `planner.py:12–43` owns the graph and topological order. Its fresh G2 session created `ARCHITECTURE.md` on its own, a positive proactive documentation result. G2 `planner.py:48–77` and `policy.py:41–58` explain retention/filtering and freeze prerequisites.
- Both checklist G1 arms created `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `TEST-REPORT.md`, and local tests, then finished 18/18. Both G2 sessions successfully read both G1 documents and their test source, in the original worktrees. This confirms user-process guidance alone can cause useful project artifacts and visible consumption. In r-6ABuMo checklist G1, `ARCHITECTURE.md:40–44` and `journal.py:29–35` classify a self-loop as malformed shape. The black-box supplemental test returns `invalid-change` where a cycle anywhere should return `dependency-cycle`. The documentation is explicit but codifies the wrong boundary.
- Both Building-loop G1 arms created real architecture and ledger contents using the native role flow, reached all 18 signed tests, passed two review roles and closed. r-6ABuMo puts graph logic in `planner.py:24–79`, explains replay conflict in `journal.py:58–78`, and connects rollback and quota behavior to the implementation in `planner.py:94–108`. r-AErMFD explains actual rollback/budget in `planner.py:84–95` and replay conflict in `journal.py:58–64`, yet the G1 architecture at line 7 wrongly says `release.py` calls policy, journal and planner directly. The generated static import section and actual `release.py:11` show release imports planner only. Both native review roles accepted that contradiction.

## Second stage final standard snapshots

- Both ordinary arms reach 21/21 in the original worktree with a distinct session, despite lack of handoff notes. They achieved 6/9 and 9/9 additional clearly scoped checks. r-6ABuMo still crashes on unhashable invalid environment values and keeps graph/order inside `journal.py:95–128`. r-AErMFD validates malformed environment types and retains graph ownership in planner. The latter fresh session created its own architecture artifact.
- Both checklist arms reused actual G1 documentation. r-6ABuMo stayed at unchanged 16/21 at 210 seconds and terminal cap. Its carried `TEST-REPORT.md:50–53` still says G2 is unpublished. r-AErMFD was 0/21 during edits at the 210-second checkpoint and recovered to 21/21 at cap. That arm updated `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PLAN-G2.md` and `TEST-REPORT.md`, with 6/9 supplementary checks. An old file read or a well-structured current report is positive evidence of access, not a standalone verdict on behavior.
- r-AErMFD checklist modified the G1 placeholder `CHANGE-G2.md` as part of its G1 behavior. The external owner replaced it with the exact common G2 requirement before each G2 session. The added G1 text is neither the initial input nor the G2 requirement.

## Second stage final Building-loop snapshots

- Both run directories continued in the original worktree after a closed G1. Distinct G2 owner sessions read the byte-identical G1 architecture and ledger, and the fresh executors received byte-identical G1 sources for all four modules. The G2 source hash binds a distinct final signed candidate in each. Both kept all 16 applicable earlier behaviors and passed all five current tests by 210 seconds. These results establish actual file-driven continuation.
- Both G2 native work units remained blocked. r-6ABuMo passed the first review and reached independent review, but an audit submit at 326.225 seconds lacked file rows for `journal.py`, `planner.py`, and `policy.py`; the audit resumed multiple times, with native blocked state at the 420.015-second cap. r-AErMFD repeated first-review submissions at 237.431 and 274.340 seconds without all four required architecture sections and without sufficient actual source evidence. It exhausted the 16 exploratory probes earlier, and the mode returned with native blocked state at 328.752 seconds. These are observed record/path failures. They do not show that code failed fixed tests or that two user instructions directly conflicted.
- Both G2 architecture documents record freeze, three-unit quota and rollback retention. r-AErMFD `modules/architecture.md:7` carries its G1 direct-call error forward even though the source and static inventory still show `release.py` imports and calls only planner. Both G2 sources have substantive comments on retained dependencies, exact reverse rollback and replay-before-budget. r-6ABuMo `planner.py:119–145` explains each branch and safety constraint, r-AErMFD `planner.py:71–83,114–131` and `policy.py:9–13,54–78` explain the closure, rollback-only validation and production freeze. No inference is made from annotation volume.
- Both G2 final AST import checks and I/O checks are 4/4. G2 additional unambiguous black-box cases are 6/9 and 9/9, exactly matching ordinary standard on these two replications. r-6ABuMo crashes on the same invalid environment shapes as the ordinary sample, even with 21/21 fixed tests. Production freeze versus malformed budget and retention through an unapplied middle node are separately recorded exploratory cases.

## Additional measures

Count source lines as context only. Do not judge documentation by the path or format. Architectural correctness additionally needs agreement among actual imports, responsibility and tested behavior. Successful source reads are tool-observable access; whether a particular statement drove a later action can remain unknown. Both coverage and journal extraction scripts are in the evidence bundle.
